title: Which Oracle replication tool fits you?

questions.q: What job do you need done?
questions.hint: The post says there is no single best Oracle replication tool, because the tools answer different questions.

options.label: A standby copy of a whole Oracle database
options.why: you want a full Oracle-to-Oracle copy

options.label: Send changes to other systems or a lake
options.why: you want changes sent to other systems

options.label: Two-way replication or a read/write replica
options.why: you need two-way or read/write replication (GoldenGate or SharePlex)

options.label: Oracle plus mainframe or other legacy sources
options.why: you have mainframe and other legacy sources

options.label: A scheduled copy of Oracle tables into a lake
options.why: you want a scheduled copy of Oracle tables

options.label: Another Oracle database
options.why: your target is another Oracle database

options.label: Iceberg tables in a lake
options.why: the post lists Iceberg routes for these tools

options.label: A vendor runs it for me
options.why: you want a vendor to run it

options.label: My team runs it, open source
options.why: you can run an open-source tool yourself (Debezium with Kafka, or OLake Go)

options.label: Either, if the fit is right

questions.q: How do you want to pay?

options.label: I need a public price
options.why: Oracle, Fivetran, AWS and Google publish prices, and Debezium and OLake Go have free open-source licences; Qlik, Confluent, SharePlex and Striim say contact us or not published

options.label: I can talk to sales
options.why: a quote from the vendor is fine

options.label: Pay by usage
options.why: you pay by rows, GiB or hours

questions.q: What is your Oracle licence situation?

options.label: No extra Oracle licences
options.why: Confluent says its XStream route is covered, and Debezium can use LogMiner. Ask every vendor about the logging setting

options.label: Standard Edition 2
options.why: the post lists Active Data Guard as an extra-cost option on Enterprise Edition, so check the rest with each vendor

dataguard.name: Oracle Active Data Guard
dataguard.summary: Copies a whole Oracle database to a standby Oracle database.
dataguard.bestWhen: You want disaster recovery or read offload inside Oracle on Enterprise Edition.
dataguard.watchOut: It copies a whole Oracle database to another Oracle database, and the post lists no lake or other database engine as a target.

goldengate.name: Oracle GoldenGate
goldengate.summary: Oracle's own tool for moving changes to many targets, including two-way replication.
goldengate.bestWhen: You run a large Oracle estate, need low-downtime moves or two-way replication, and have the budget.
goldengate.watchOut: Licences are priced per processor or user at both ends of the copy, and Iceberg writing lives in a separate product.

qlik.name: Qlik Replicate
qlik.summary: Reads Oracle with LogMiner or its own log reader, and also takes mainframe sources.
qlik.bestWhen: You have Oracle plus mainframe sources and are happy to talk to sales.
qlik.watchOut: Prices are not published, so you cannot budget without a sales call.

dms.name: AWS DMS
dms.summary: A managed AWS service that reads Oracle with LogMiner or Binary Reader.
dms.bestWhen: Your target is on AWS and you want a managed service.
dms.watchOut: Iceberg is not on AWS's list of DMS target endpoints, so it takes two steps with S3 files and Glue jobs.

datastream.name: Google Datastream
datastream.summary: Google's service for Oracle changes, billed per GiB processed.
datastream.bestWhen: You are on Google Cloud and land data in BigQuery.
datastream.watchOut: Iceberg streaming is append-only, and large objects arrive as NULL unless you set a flag.

debezium.name: Debezium
debezium.summary: Open source with a free licence. You choose LogMiner, XStream or OpenLogReplicator.
debezium.bestWhen: You already run Kafka and can operate it.
debezium.watchOut: You pay for servers and staff, and the first snapshot can hit an ORA-01555 error.

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A fully managed service with several Oracle reading methods.
fivetran.bestWhen: You want someone else to run Oracle replication and can budget for Monthly Active Rows.
fivetran.watchOut: Oracle sources need the Enterprise or Business Critical plan, and so does Hybrid Deployment, which runs in your own environment.

confluent.name: Confluent Oracle XStream connector
confluent.summary: A managed connector that sends Oracle changes into Kafka topics.
confluent.bestWhen: Kafka is your hub and you want XStream without buying GoldenGate.
confluent.watchOut: It writes changes to Kafka topics, the price is not published, and the licence claim is Confluent's own.

striim.name: Striim
striim.summary: Reads Oracle with LogMiner or its OJet reader, and can read GoldenGate trail files.
striim.bestWhen: Oracle volume is high and you are fine talking to sales.
striim.watchOut: Its docs name Google Cloud Storage as the only supported data lake for the Iceberg Writer (S3 Tables has its own writer), and paid prices say contact us.

shareplex.name: Quest SharePlex
shareplex.summary: Replicates Oracle to Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Kafka and Parquet files, with two-way support.
shareplex.bestWhen: You want Oracle high availability or a move to PostgreSQL.
shareplex.watchOut: Quest's page lists Oracle and PostgreSQL as sources, the price is not published, and the post found no Iceberg target.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: Open source tool that copies Oracle tables into Apache Iceberg or Parquet with Full Refresh or Full Refresh + Incremental syncs.
olake.bestWhen: You want scheduled copies of Oracle tables in a lake on storage you control.
olake.watchOut: Oracle is read with Full Refresh or Full Refresh + Incremental syncs, so it suits scheduled table copies.
